title: Newmark Program Allows Customers To Donate To UConn Athletics

body_markdown:
James Ritman, Newmark Executive Vice President and Managing Director of the company’s Stamford office (center), and members of UConn’s men’s basketball team at the 3rd Annual UConn Legends Golf Tournament at Greenwich Country Club. Photo courtesy of Newmark


STAMFORD – Newmark has kicked off a strategic program with the University of Connecticut Athletics Foundation where it will donate a portion of fees generated from its commercial real estate services to support UConn’s athletic programs and student-athletes.


The ongoing donation enables UConn-affiliated companies or clients to allocate a share of transaction- and advisory-related fees generated by Newmark toward UConn Athletics, academic and research initiatives or the university’s general endowment.


“Newmark looks forward to working with companies, investors, and real estate owners to support and invest in Connecticut’s flagship university,” said James Ritman, executive vice president and managing director of the Newmark Stamford office and head of the program. “Newmark is honored to donate a portion of revenue on these transactions back to UConn.”


Since opening its Connecticut office in 1993, Newmark has long been committed to the state’s growth. In a statement, the company said by brokering headquarters transactions for Fortune 500 companies and attracting billions in real estate investment, Newmark has established itself as one of the leading commercial real estate advisors in the state. The collaboration with UConn reflects the firm’s continued commitment to Connecticut and its longstanding belief in giving back.


“This program with Newmark is an exciting new opportunity that speaks to their dedication to making a real difference,” said UConn COO Jason Butikofer. “Knowing that businesses engaging Newmark’s real estate services can direct a portion of those proceeds to UConn Athletics is truly meaningful, and we are excited about the impact this program can have for our student-athletes and programs.”
